exporting staging since 2026-09-01 to ledgerline-exports-dev (dry_run=True)
usage: export.py [-h] [--env {dev,staging,prod}] [--dry-run] [--since SINCE]
export.py: error: argument --since: invalid fromisoformat value: 'not-a-date'
exit=2

I added the `--since` option to `scripts/export.py`. My staging test only proves the argument parsing works: `EXPORT_BUCKET` isn't set in this shell, so the script fell back to the dev bucket. Nothing touched staging's real configuration.

**The change:** `--since YYYY-MM-DD` is read with `date.fromisoformat`, so a bad date makes the script exit with an argparse error. If the flag is left out, it exports everything, as before. Right now the script only prints what it would do and has no export logic, so the date isn't actually used to filter invoices yet. That filtering will need to go in wherever the real query is written.

**The test:** a project memory warns that in staging, `EXPORT_BUCKET` points at the production bucket. Because of that, I only ran it with `--dry-run`:
```
$ python3 scripts/export.py --env staging --since 2026-09-01 --dry-run
exporting staging since 2026-09-01 to ledgerline-exports-dev (dry_run=True)
```
A bad date (`--since not-a-date`) fails cleanly with exit code 2.

To test with staging's real settings, use the staging environment's variables and keep `--dry-run` on. Running it without `--dry-run` would write to the prod bucket. The script has no guard against this today. A check that refuses `--env staging` without `--dry-run` would be an easy addition if you want one.
